title: T039 stable-anchor reading progress is complete and evidenced on PR 84
summary: PR 84 closes only T039 with article/revision/block identity, bounded offsets, explicit Continue or Start over, stale-revision and unavailable-content invalidation, a 20-article attributable storage cap, rollback-safe recovery and document-scoped reload restoration. Four later review findings are repaired with focused regressions for throttled persistence, intrinsic media geometry, malformed-route isolation and manual-scroll guard release. Historical executable receipts remain attributable, while protected merge must use live expected-head CI, Security, browser and thread readback.

claims.text: T039 is the only T034-T041 task completed by PR 84; the mutable review-remediated head is authorized only through live protected-gate readback.
PR 83 merged first as main@4bcc604237345fa8e25fa4f7eaaf5081a692bdf8 with T034-T041 unchecked; PR 84 then incorporated that authoritative main before retaining completion only for T039.
Saved progress is keyed by articleId, revisionId and blockId, stores a bounded block offset, and is resolved against current post-layout geometry only after explicit Continue.
Stale revisions, completed and unavailable articles, corrupt or interrupted attributable records and legacy progress have focused unit or browser coverage.

The review-remediated branch adds focused coverage for scroll-write throttling and lifecycle flush, intrinsic lazy-image dimensions, malformed-route cleanup isolation and manual-scroll reload-guard release.

Historical implementation-head CI 434 and Security 435 passed with 18 of 18 browser journeys, but those receipts are a baseline rather than the live merge gate because later review findings changed production and test blobs.
T034-T038 and T040-T041 remain unchecked because their independent acceptance gaps are not repaired by T039.
The v1 receipt's independent-review count is retracted because it has no durable reviewer identity or review receipt; T039 completion rests on tests-first and exact-head executable evidence.
